name: Badlands
notes: Eroded clay and shale slopes mostly bare, with junipers in ravines, low sage and prickly pear on benches and short grasses in the flats; Dakota/Montana badlands with Bardenas Reales (Spain) and Patagonian analogues.

canopy.name: Rocky Mountain juniper
canopy.source: Juniperus scopulorum (Rocky Mountain juniper), N American plains breaks and badland ravines, 5-12 m — USDA PLANTS

canopy.name: Plains cottonwood
canopy.source: Populus deltoides, badland creek bottoms, 15-30 m — USDA PLANTS

canopy.name: Aleppo pine
canopy.source: Pinus halepensis, Bardenas Reales and Spanish gypsum badlands, 8-20 m — Euro+Med PlantBase

shrub.name: Silver sagebrush
shrub.source: Artemisia cana, northern Great Plains badland flats and draws, silver shrub 0.5-1.5 m — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Skunkbush sumac
shrub.source: Rhus trilobata, western N America ravines and rocky slopes, 1-2.5 m, red autumn foliage — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Plains prickly pear
shrub.source: Opuntia polyacantha, badland benches and clay slopes, 20-50 cm clumps — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Rubber rabbitbrush
shrub.source: Ericameria nauseosa, badland washes and disturbed slopes, 0.6-2 m — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Greasewood
shrub.source: Sarcobatus vermiculatus, saline badland bottoms, 1-2.5 m — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Soapweed yucca
shrub.source: Yucca glauca, dry badland slopes of the Great Plains, 0.5-1.2 m — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Western wheatgrass
ground.source: Pascopyrum smithii, dominant grass of northern badland flats on clay, 0.3-0.9 m — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Blue grama
ground.source: Bouteloua gracilis, badland benches and prairie tables, 15-40 cm — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Little bluestem
ground.source: Schizachyrium scoparium, badland slopes and tables, 0.5-1 m, red-brown in autumn — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Gumbo evening primrose
ground.source: Oenothera caespitosa, bare clay badland slopes of western N America, rosette 10-30 cm with white flowers — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Esparto grass
ground.source: Macrochloa tenacissima, Spanish gypsum badlands, tussock 0.5-1.2 m — Euro+Med PlantBase

special.note: Catalogue plants (data/plants) whose band centres fall inside this biome's climate; computed, informational. Phase 6 may raise their density here so they are findable.

associations.name: Rocky Mountain juniper ravine woodland
associations.where: shaded north-facing draws and ravine heads with extra runoff moisture
associations.source: Butler et al. 1986 Badlands NP vegetation; USNVC Juniperus scopulorum badlands woodland

associations.name: Western wheatgrass-blue grama flat
associations.where: gentle clay flats and tablelands between the eroded slopes
associations.source: Kuchler 1964 wheatgrass-needlegrass; Butler et al. 1986 Badlands NP

associations.name: Silver sagebrush-greasewood bench
associations.where: low benches and alkaline flats along drainages, heavy clay, seasonal moisture
associations.source: Hansen & Hoffman 1988 Sarcobatus-Artemisia cana bottomland; USNVC

associations.name: Prickly pear-yucca eroded slope
associations.where: bare clay and shale slopes and sod tables, dry and unstable
associations.source: Butler et al. 1986 Badlands NP sparse vegetation; Hansen & Hoffman 1988

associations.name: Plains cottonwood draw
associations.where: creek bottoms and wet draws with groundwater at the base of the badlands
associations.source: Hansen & Hoffman 1988 Populus deltoides floodplain woodland

associations.name: Aleppo pine-esparto gully scrub
associations.where: clay gullies of Bardenas Reales, dry Mediterranean semi-desert, scattered pine on gully sides
associations.source: Rivas-Martinez Pinus halepensis-Stipa tenacissima steppe, Ebro valley badlands
